issues.legal_issue: The period for executing a granted mining lease runs from the grantee’s receipt of the sanction, and an application for the same area made before that period expires is premature.
material_facts: A mining lease had been sanctioned to an earlier applicant, who received notice of the sanction after it was issued.
The earlier applicant did not execute the formal lease within the prescribed period, and no extension was shown.
A later applicant sought the overlapping area before the prescribed period, calculated from receipt of the sanction, had expired.
issues.conclusion: The application made before the prescribed period expired was premature and was rightly rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 19(1) of the Rajasthan Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1977 requires execution of the formal lease within three months from the grantee’s receipt of the sanction, not from the date the lease was granted. If the lease is not executed in that period, the grant is deemed revoked, subject to the rule’s proviso permitting an extension in the specified circumstances. No earlier case is relied on for this issue.

rule.if: mining_lease_regrant_case and prior_grantee_received_sanction and formal_lease_not_executed and no_execution_extension and later_application_before_receipt_based_deadline

predicates.mining_lease_regrant_case: The proceeding concerns an application to obtain an area previously covered by a mining-lease grant.
predicates.prior_grantee_received_sanction: The person to whom the earlier lease was granted received notice of the sanction.
predicates.formal_lease_not_executed: The earlier grantee did not execute the formal lease within the required period.
predicates.no_execution_extension: The authority did not extend the time for executing the formal lease.
predicates.later_application_before_receipt_based_d: A later applicant applied for the area before the required period, counted from the earlier grantee’s receipt of the sanction, had expired.

issues.definition: When a later applicant seeks an area covered by an unexecuted grant before the receipt-based execution period expires and that period has not been extended, the later application is premature.

issues.legal_issue: The register-entry and waiting-period requirements for regrant of land previously held under a mining lease do not apply when a grant is revoked because the grantee failed to execute the formal lease.
material_facts: The earlier grantee received a lease sanction but did not execute a formal lease, so the grant was deemed revoked.
The area had not been held under an executed mining lease pursuant to that grant.
The later applicant relied on the absence of an entry and waiting period under the rules governing regrant of areas previously held under a mining lease.
issues.conclusion: Rules 56 and 57 of the 1977 Rules did not apply to the area covered by the unexecuted grant that had been revoked.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 56 and 57 address areas previously held under a mining lease; they do not extend to a grant revoked under Rule 19(1) before a formal lease was executed. Rule 57 covers the same field as Rule 56 and does not broaden it. Rule 59(1) of the 1986 Rules, which expressly addresses revoked grants, illustrates the distinction. No earlier case is relied on for this issue.

predicates.mining_lease_regrant_case: The proceeding concerns an application to obtain an area previously covered by a mining-lease grant.
predicates.prior_grant_revoked_without_executed_lea: The earlier grant was revoked after its grantee failed to execute the formal lease.
predicates.prior_area_not_held_under_formal_lease: The area was not previously held under an executed mining lease.

issues.definition: When a mining-lease grant is revoked before a formal lease is executed and the area was not held under an executed lease, the register-entry and waiting-period requirement does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: When the rules do not specify when an area covered by a deemed-revoked grant becomes available to third parties, an administrative order may set a publicly announced availability date, and an application made before that date is premature.
material_facts: The grant of a mining lease was deemed revoked because the grantee did not execute the formal lease.
The applicable rules did not specify when an area covered by such a revoked grant became available for regrant.
An administrative order declared the area available for reallocation after a notice period, and the later applicant applied before that period had elapsed.
issues.conclusion: The administrative order was consistent with the rules, and the application made before the announced availability date was premature.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 19(1) provides for automatic revocation but the 1977 Rules do not specify when the area thereby becomes available to third parties. Because a mining lease is a privilege of the State and applicants must have an equal opportunity to apply, availability cannot rest on internal communications unknown to potential applicants; public notice is needed. In the absence of a conflicting rule, an administrative order may fix the availability date. The Court also referred to the 1976 departmental circular as guidance for notice and to Rule 59(1) of the 1986 Rules, which later expressly provided for public notice and a waiting period. No earlier case is relied on for this issue.

rule.if: mining_lease_regrant_case and grant_deemed_revoked and rules_silent_on_third_party_availability_date and administrative_order_publicly_announced_availability_date and application_before_announced_availability_date

predicates.mining_lease_regrant_case: The proceeding concerns an application to obtain an area previously covered by a mining-lease grant.
predicates.grant_deemed_revoked: The earlier grant ended by deemed revocation after the grantee failed to execute the formal lease.
predicates.rules_silent_on_third_party_availability: The applicable rules did not specify when the area became available to third parties after that deemed revocation.
predicates.administrative_order_publicly_announced_: An administrative order announced that the area would become available for reallocation after a stated notice period.
predicates.application_before_announced_availabilit: An applicant applied for the area before the availability date announced in the administrative order.

issues.definition: When the rules leave the third-party availability date unspecified, a public administrative announcement may set that date, and an application filed before it is premature.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising constitutional writ review may consider a relevant document filed with the writ petition even if it was not placed before the administrative authorities.
material_facts: A document bearing on when the earlier grantee received the lease sanction was filed with the writ petition.
The document had not been presented in the earlier administrative proceedings.
A judge declined to consider it on the ground that it had not been before those authorities.
issues.conclusion: The document’s absence from the earlier administrative proceedings did not prevent the writ court from considering it.
issues.legal_principle: In the exercise of jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court could consider relevant material filed with the writ petition; the fact that the material had not been placed before the administrative authorities did not, by itself, bar consideration. No earlier case is relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_review: The proceeding is a court’s review of an administrative decision under its constitutional writ jurisdiction.
predicates.relevant_document_filed_with_writ_petiti: A party filed a document with the writ petition that bears on an issue in the case.
predicates.document_material_to_disputed_fact: The document is relevant to a fact disputed in the proceeding.
predicates.document_not_before_administrative_autho: The document was not placed before the administrative authorities that made or reviewed the decision.

issues.definition: In constitutional writ review, a relevant document filed with the petition may be considered even if the administrative authorities did not have it.
